lesson.text: Quick memory: what do you do if a dog runs at you? (Be a tree.) Today: how dogs talk with their bodies, the farm, wasps and snakes.
A relaxed dog: a loose body, a soft face, a gently wagging tail. A dog saying 'leave me alone': a stiff body, a hard stare, lips pulled back, the tail held high. Give it space.
Most dogs don't like hugs: arms round the neck feel like being trapped. Ask the owner, let it sniff your hand, stroke its side.
Near cows with calves, walk calmly round the edge of the field. Never walk behind a horse. Wasps: move away slowly, no swatting.
A snake on the path: step back slowly and leave it alone. A swollen face or trouble breathing after a sting: call {number}.
Try it in the world: open the park, the farm and the hill path. Next: the hills, guard dogs and stings, on the Big track.

choices: a stiff body and a hard stare

items: walk away slowly when it goes
